verdicts.title: Validate buffer length at the top of Plan.unpack_tuple so both tiers reject wrong-length input with a uniform ValueError
verdicts.issues: Verified end-to-end on an isolated copy (before-snippet matches current source verbatim; all BEFORE/AFTER repro outputs reproduced exactly; 854 passed pristine AND patched; no struct.error catchers anywhere in repo/tests; legacy aggregate does NOT route through unpack_tuple, so the no-sync claim holds). Nits for revision, none blocking: (1) PERF: the guard costs more than the claimed 'one len() comparison' because self.num_bytes is a PROPERTY (Python-level descriptor call). Measured (min of 5x200k, two runs): aligned-tier unpack_tuple ~117 -> ~171 ns/call (+~45%), shiftmask unpack_tuple ~478 -> ~606 ns/call, and the shiftmask iter_tuples bulk loop (which calls unpack_tuple per record) ~64us -> ~72us per 100 records (+~11%). The aligned iter_unpack bulk path is untouched as claimed, and Struct.parse regression is within noise, but the fix should use `len(data) * 8 != self.num_bits` (direct __slots__ access) or precompute a _num_bytes slot in __init__ -- pack_tuple's len(self.fields) guard measured ~zero added cost, confirming the property is the culprit. (2) Disclosed-but-understated regression: a memoryview with itemsize>1 previously decoded CORRECTLY on both tiers (bytes()/struct.unpack flatten to bytes); the guard now falsely rejects it because len() counts items ('expected 2 bytes, got 1' for a 2-byte array('H') view). The risk note frames this as hypothetical; it is a real (if exotic) input that used to work. Casting via memoryview(data).cast('B') or comparing nbytes would fix it, at perf cost -- at minimum the risk wording should say 'previously worked, now falsely rejected'. (3) The iter_tuples side effect does NOT unify tiers: after the patch, shiftmask over-count raises ValueError but the struct tier STILL silently truncates (count=4 over a 2-record buffer yields 2 tuples) or raises struct.error when the remainder is not a multiple of the record size. So over-count behavior remains cross-tier inconsistent -- correctly deferred to bugs.md finding 26, but the 'beneficial side effect' framing oversells partial coverage; the finding-26 group must own the unification. No current caller is affected: Array.parse pre-validates length so its explicit count always fits exactly, and all tests use in-range counts.

verdicts.title: Validate value count at the top of Plan.pack_tuple so both tiers reject wrong-arity sequences with a uniform ValueError
verdicts.issues: Verified: before-snippet matches current source verbatim; the bonus claim is real (pristine aligned tier pack_tuple([5,6,7]) returns b'\x05\x06' via the wrap-retry's zip-truncated _wrap_values; patched raises ValueError on both tiers, covering both the direct and wrap-retry paths); wrap semantics intact (right-arity out-of-range [0x105,-1] still packs '05ff', test_plan_pack_tuple_wraps green); 854 passed patched. Guard cost measured ~zero (shiftmask pack ~435 ns unchanged; struct pack within noise) because len(self.fields) is a direct slot access -- no perf concern. One accuracy nit in the risks text: it claims 'generators were never reliably supported', but empirically an iterator/generator of correct arity produced CORRECT bytes on BOTH tiers pre-patch (struct.pack(*gen) star-materializes; the shiftmask zip consumes it) -- e.g. pristine pack_tuple(iter([1,564])) -> '4123'. After the guard these raise TypeError from len(). The regression is loud, the signature declares Sequence, and no internal caller passes iterators, so acceptable for a single-user library, but the risk note should state the old behavior worked rather than imply it was already broken.
